//: NOT A PACKAGE. No name, no version, no dependencies, never installed. It exists to declare the MODULE KIND of the .js files under .claude/ and nothing else. Node resolves a .js file's module kind from the NEAREST package.json above it, so this answers for .claude/** without making any claim about the project at the repo root. WHY: dev-standards M-KIT-17 / L-94 — the kit's hooks use static `import`, and in a typeless package they load ONLY because Node >= 22.7 detects module syntax and reparses them, printing MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON to stderr on every invocation. That compensation is version-dependent: on an older Node the same file is a SyntaxError at load, and a hook that fails to load gates nothing. WHY HERE AND NOT IN hooks/: a statusline or any other .claude-level script that imports a hook as a library would otherwise be CommonJS reaching into an ES module, trading one runtime compensation for another instead of removing it. WHAT WAS WEIGHED INSTEAD: renaming every hook to .mjs — settings.json registers hooks BY PATH and check-hook-registration reconciles that path, so it is four files plus a settings edit, and a rename is a code change until proven otherwise — or "type": "module" at the repo root, which is a claim about the whole project made to fix files under .claude. This is neither, and it is one file to delete if it is ever wrong. IF YOUR .claude/ SCRIPTS ARE CommonJS, set "commonjs" here rather than deleting the file: the declaration is the point, and an explicit kind is what stops the runtime guessing.
